roles.name: Bug Investigator
roles.prompt: From the user's problem description, investigate the failure. Reproduce it if possible (run the failing command, test, or scenario), read the relevant code, and trace the root cause rather than the surface symptom. Do not fix anything yet. Write artifacts/DIAGNOSIS.md with: the observed problem, reproduction steps, the root cause with file/line evidence, other places the same defect pattern may exist, and a proposed fix approach.

roles.name: Bug Fixer
roles.prompt: Read artifacts/DIAGNOSIS.md. Fix the root cause with the smallest change that actually resolves it - do not paper over symptoms, silence errors, or add workarounds that leave the underlying defect in place. Fix any other occurrences of the same defect identified in the diagnosis. Write artifacts/FIX_NOTES.md with what was changed and why, how the fix addresses the root cause, and anything intentionally left alone.

roles.name: Fix Verifier
roles.prompt: Read artifacts/DIAGNOSIS.md and artifacts/FIX_NOTES.md. Re-run the original reproduction to confirm the problem is gone, then run the relevant test suite to check for regressions. If no test covered this bug, add one that fails without the fix and passes with it. Write artifacts/FIX_VERIFICATION.md with commands run, results, the new/updated tests, and any remaining failures.

roles.name: Fix Reviewer
roles.prompt: Read all prior artifacts and the actual diff. Verify the fix addresses the root cause from the diagnosis rather than masking symptoms, check for side effects or regressions the change could introduce elsewhere, and confirm the verification was adequate. Write artifacts/FIX_REVIEW.md with findings, risks, and an approval status.

Root cause: the remaining bug is not stale `active_scatter_id`; it is GPU scatter compositing. `ScatterCompositeRenderer` owns one shared `uniform_buffer` for `target_rect`, and every `ScatterRenderTarget` bind group references that same buffer. With two cached/offscreen scatter widgets in one frame, both draws can use the last-written rectangle, so the left plot texture gets drawn into the right plot area.

Key evidence:

Proposed fix: move the composite uniform buffer into `ScatterRenderTarget` or otherwise make placement data per draw/per target. Keep compositor pipeline/layout/sampler shared, but do not share mutable placement uniforms across scatter targets. Verification must include pixel-based adjacent plot checks, since the existing pass marker only checks state and misses wrong on-screen placement.

# Diagnosis: Adjacent Scatter Plot Overlay

## Observed Problem

On the professional demo's `3D Explore` tab, the left plot is a `Scatter3D` and the smaller right plot is a `ScatterPlot2D`. `ScatterPlot2D` is not a separate renderer; it subclasses `Scatter3D` and uses the same native `scatter_3d` widget/runtime. When multiple scatter surfaces are visible, clicking/dragging outside the left plot or interacting with the neighboring plot can cause the cached/offscreen-rendered plot textures to composite into the same screen rectangle, visually combining/overlaying the two plots.

The existing adjacent plot probe did not catch this because it checks stable data signatures and `active_scatter_id`, not whether the composited pixels land in the correct rectangle.

# Fix Notes: Adjacent Scatter Composite Overlay

## Root Cause

The remaining professional demo overlay bug was caused by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
owning one mutable composite uniform buffer for `target_rect`. Every cached scatter
render target had a bind group pointing at that same buffer, so multiple offscreen
scatter composites encoded in one frame could all observe the last-written placement
rectangle.

That made the left plot texture render into the right plot rectangle when two
cached scatter widgets were visible.

  and into each `ScatterRenderTarget` in `native/src/runtime.rs`.
- Kept the compositor pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared.
- Changed each scatter render target bind group to bind its own
  `composite_uniform_buffer`.
- Changed the render loop to call `target.update_composite_uniforms(...)` before
  drawing that target's composite bind group.
- Added pixel-level validation for the `adjacent-scatter-interaction` visual audit
  in `tools/visual_audit.py`. The validator uses scatter viewport rectangles from
  the debug snapshot and checks that both visible plot viewports contain plot
  pixels, catching the previous state-only blind spot.

# Fix Notes: Adjacent Scatter Composite Overlay

## Root Cause

The remaining professional demo overlay bug was caused by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
owning one mutable composite uniform buffer for `target_rect`. Every cached scatter
render target had a bind group pointing at that same buffer, so multiple offscreen
scatter composites encoded in one frame could all observe the last-written placement
rectangle.

That made the left plot texture render into the right plot rectangle when two
cached scatter widgets were visible.

## Code Changes

- Moved the mutable composite placement uniform out of `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
  and into each `ScatterRenderTarget` in `native/src/runtime.rs`.
- Kept the compositor pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared.
- Changed each scatter render target bind group to bind its own
  `composite_uniform_buffer`.
- Changed the render loop to call `target.update_composite_uniforms(...)` before
  drawing that target's composite bind group.
- Added pixel-level validation for the `adjacent-scatter-interaction` visual audit
  in `tools/visual_audit.py`. The validator uses scatter viewport rectangles from
  the debug snapshot and checks that both visible plot viewports contain plot
  pixels, catching the previous state-only blind spot.
- Added a focused unit test in `tests/test_visual_audit.py` that fails when the
  left adjacent scatter viewport is blank.

        self.x = np.cos(theta) * radius - np.float32(8.0)

def find_probe_window() -> int | None:
    user32 = ctypes.windll.user32
    pid = os.getpid()
    found = ctypes.c_void_p(0)

    @ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(ctypes.c_bool, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_void_p)
    def enum_proc(hwnd: int, _param: int) -> bool:
        if not user32.IsWindowVisible(hwnd):
            return True
        window_pid = ctypes.c_ulong()
        user32.GetWindowThreadProcessId(hwnd, ctypes.byref(window_pid))
        if window_pid.value != pid:
            return True
        length = user32.GetWindowTextLengthW(hwnd)
        if length <= 0:

        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(length + 1)
        user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, length + 1)

            return False
        return True

    user32.EnumWindows(enum_proc, 0)
    return int(found.value) if found.value else None

    ctypes.windll.user32.SetCursorPos(sx, sy)
    time.sleep(0.04)


def mouse_event(flags: int, data: int = 0) -> None:
    ctypes.windll.user32.mouse_event(flags, 0, 0, data, 0)
    time.sleep(0.05)


def click(hwnd: int, x: float, y: float) -> None:
    send_mouse_move(hwnd, x, y)
    mouse_event(0x0002)
    mouse_event(0x0004)

# Fix Notes: Adjacent Scatter Composite Overlay

## Root Cause

The remaining professional demo overlay bug was caused by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
owning one mutable composite uniform buffer for `target_rect`. Every cached scatter
render target had a bind group pointing at that same buffer, so multiple offscreen
scatter composites encoded in one frame could all observe the last-written placement
rectangle.

That made the left plot texture render into the right plot rectangle when two
cached scatter widgets were visible.

## Code Changes

- Moved the mutable composite placement uniform out of `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
  and into each `ScatterRenderTarget` in `native/src/runtime.rs`.
- Kept the compositor pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared.
- Changed each scatter render target bind group to bind its own
  `composite_uniform_buffer`.
- Changed the render loop to call `target.update_composite_uniforms(...)` before
  drawing that target's composite bind group.
- Added pixel-level validation for the `adjacent-scatter-interaction` visual audit
  in `tools/visual_audit.py`. The validator uses scatter viewport rectangles from
  the debug snapshot and checks that both visible plot viewports contain plot
  pixels, catching the previous state-only blind spot.
- Added a focused unit test in `tests/test_visual_audit.py` that fails when the
  left adjacent scatter viewport is blank.

  drawing that target's composite bind group.

## Root Cause

The remaining professional demo overlay bug was caused by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
owning one mutable composite uniform buffer for `target_rect`. Every cached scatter
render target had a bind group pointing at that same buffer, so multiple offscreen
scatter composites encoded in one frame could all observe the last-written placement
rectangle.

That made the left plot texture render into the right plot rectangle when two
cached scatter widgets were visible.

## Code Changes

- Moved the mutable composite placement uniform out of `ScatterCompositeRenderer`
  and into each `ScatterRenderTarget` in `native/src/runtime.rs`.
- Kept the compositor pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared.
- Changed each scatter render target bind group to bind its own
  `composite_uniform_buffer`.
- Changed the render loop to call `target.update_composite_uniforms(...)` before
  drawing that target's composite bind group.
- Added pixel-level validation for the `adjacent-scatter-interaction` visual audit
  in `tools/visual_audit.py`. The validator uses scatter viewport rectangles from
  the debug snapshot and checks that both visible plot viewports contain plot
  pixels, catching the previous state-only blind spot.
- Added a focused unit test in `tests/test_visual_audit.py` that fails when the
  left adjacent scatter viewport is blank.

## Rebuild

The native library was rebuilt and copied into the workspace Python package path:

```powershell

$env:PYO3_PYTHON = "C:\Users\nashk\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe"
cargo build --manifest-path native/Cargo.toml --release
Copy-Item native\target\release\_dragongui.dll python\dragongui\_dragongui.pyd -Force
```


## Observed Problem

The professional demo's `3D Explore` tab still has two visible scatter plots: a large left `Scatter3D` and a smaller right `ScatterPlot2D`. The user's report matches the current source behavior: when the cached/offscreen scatter path is active, the left plot's rendered data can be composited into the right plot's screen rectangle, visually combining the two plots.

I reproduced the same class of failure with the adjacent scatter probe screenshot at:

```text
artifacts/visual_audit/screenshots/adjacent-scatter-interaction-1120x720.png
```

In that capture, the left plot panel is mostly blank except for edge labels, while the 3D plot grid/points are drawn over the right plot. This is the visual overlay failure, even though the probe's debug-state checks say the two widget ids still have distinct data.

## Reproduction Steps

```powershell
$py='C:\Users\nashk\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe'
& $py tools\visual_audit.py --target adjacent-scatter-interaction --sizes 1120x720 --append --wait-ms 2500 --timeout-ms 16000
```

- The probe prints `ADJACENT_SCATTER_INTERACTION_PASS`, but this pass marker is misleading for this bug. It only verifies state signatures and `active_scatter_id`, not pixel placement.

The relevant snapshot confirms both visible scatters were using the cached/composite path in the same frame:

- `adjacent-right-scatter`: `last_render_cache_hit=True`, `last_render_composite_ms > 0`

  - right clip roughly `x=808, y=54, w=306, h=666`

## Root Cause

The previous fix addressed stale pointer state (`active_scatter_id`) but did not fix the remaining compositor bug. The scatter offscreen compositor stores the placement rectangle in one shared uniform buffer owned by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`, while each scatter render target has its own texture bind group that points back at that shared buffer.

File/line evidence:

- [examples/all_features_professional_demo.py](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/examples/all_features_professional_demo.py:579) creates the large left `Scatter3D`.
- [examples/all_features_professional_demo.py](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/examples/all_features_professional_demo.py:605) creates the right `ScatterPlot2D`.
- [python/dragongui/widgets.py](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/python/dragongui/widgets.py:11752) shows `ScatterPlot2D` subclasses `Scatter3D`, and [python/dragongui/widgets.py](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/python/dragongui/widgets.py:11755) keeps `kind = Scatter3D.kind`, so both widgets share the same native scatter runtime.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1264) defines `ScatterCompositeRenderer`; [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1268) stores a single `uniform_buffer`.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1384) binds that same compositor uniform buffer into every scatter target's composite bind group.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1426) defines `ScatterRenderTarget`; it stores only `bind_group`, dimensions, format, and revision, not a per-target/per-draw composite uniform.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1476) creates each render target bind group through the shared compositor.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13786) writes the current scatter widget's `target_rect` into the shared uniform buffer immediately before drawing that scatter target.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13800) starts the composite render pass, and [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13816) draws the target using that target's texture bind group.
- [native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl:26) uses `uniforms.target_rect` in the vertex shader to place the sampled target texture on screen.

Why this fails: multiple `queue.write_buffer` calls update the same uniform buffer while encoding a frame. The draw bind groups sample different per-widget textures, but all of them reference the same placement uniform resource. With two cached scatter widgets in one frame, later writes can make both composite draws use the last scatter's rectangle. That produces exactly the screenshot: the left scatter texture is sampled, but placed into the right scatter's rectangle, combining with the right plot.

The user trigger fits this path because clicking/dragging changes scatter interaction/cache state:

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:20719) hit-tests a scatter on mouse down.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:20724) records `active_scatter_id`.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:20783) enables interaction LOD for the active scatter.
- [native/src/scatter/mod.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/mod.rs:2239) makes `active_render_scale()` drop below full scale while LOD is active.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13698) routes render-scale cases through the offscreen target path.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13700) also allows static full-scale cached targets to be composited, so the bug can appear even when debug state says interactions are inactive.

There is a secondary invalidation risk in [native/src/scatter/mod.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/mod.rs:2319): `set_layout_rect()` intentionally keeps cached render targets valid for pure screen-position/scissor changes. That is only safe if the compositor placement state is isolated per draw. With the shared uniform, position-only cache reuse makes the wrong-rectangle failure more visible.

## Why The Prior Fix Did Not Solve It

The previous implementation added `cancel_scatter_interaction()` and expanded debug snapshots. That was useful for stale event routing, but the current screenshot and snapshot show:

- `active_scatter_id` is `null`.
- Left/right point counts, bounds, colormaps, and scalar-bar settings remain distinct.
- The visual failure still occurs because texture placement is wrong, not because plot data or widget ids are swapped.

So the bug is in GPU compositing state, not Python data reuse, widget id collision, or stale `active_scatter_id`.

## Other Places With The Same Defect Pattern

Direct same-defect pattern:

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1264) through [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1424): one `ScatterCompositeRenderer` with one mutable uniform buffer.

Any view with two or more visible `Scatter3D`/`ScatterPlot2D` widgets can exhibit this when at least two are rendered through the cached/offscreen compositor path. Known affected surfaces:

- Professional demo `3D Explore`
- `examples/css_feature_probes/adjacent_scatter_interaction_probe.py`

Other renderers are probably not affected by this exact bug. The line plot and primitive renderers use their own render paths and do not use `ScatterCompositeRenderer`.

## Proposed Fix Approach

Fix the compositor so composite placement data is not a mutable singleton shared by all scatter composites in a frame.

Preferred implementation:

1. Move the composite uniform buffer from `ScatterCompositeRenderer` into `ScatterRenderTarget`.
2. Create each `ScatterRenderTarget` with:
   - its offscreen color/depth textures,
   - its own `wgpu::Buffer` for `ScatterCompositeUniforms`,
   - a bind group that binds that target-specific uniform buffer plus the target texture view and shared sampler.
3. Replace `ScatterCompositeRenderer::update_uniforms(...)` with either:
   - `ScatterRenderTarget::update_composite_uniforms(...)`, or
   - a compositor helper that accepts `&target.uniform_buffer`.
4. In the scatter render loop, update the current target's own uniform buffer before drawing `target.bind_group`.
5. Keep the pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared in `ScatterCompositeRenderer`; only the mutable per-draw placement data needs to move.

Acceptable alternatives:

- Use a dynamic uniform buffer with one aligned offset per visible scatter in the frame.
- Use immediate/push constants for `target_rect` and `screen_size` if supported cleanly by the current wgpu/backend constraints.

- Assert each plot rectangle retains a distinct pixel signature and that left-plot pixels do not appear inside the right rectangle or vice versa.
- Keep the existing debug-state checks, but add screenshot/pixel checks because the present bug leaves state signatures correct while pixels are wrong.

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1426) defines `ScatterRenderTarget`; it stores only `bind_group`, dimensions, format, and revision, not a per-target/per-draw composite uniform.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1476) creates each render target bind group through the shared compositor.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13786) writes the current scatter widget's `target_rect` into the shared uniform buffer immediately before drawing that scatter target.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13800) starts the composite render pass, and [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13816) draws the target using that target's texture bind group.
- [native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl:26) uses `uniforms.target_rect` in the vertex shader to place the sampled target texture on screen.

Why this fails: multiple `queue.write_buffer` calls update the same uniform buffer while encoding a frame. The draw bind groups sample different per-widget textures, but all of them reference the same placement uniform resource. With two cached scatter widgets in one frame, later writes can make both composite draws use the last scatter's rectangle. - [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13698) routes render-scale cases through the offscreen target path.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13700) also allows static full-scale cached targets to be composited, so the bug can appear even when debug state says interactions are inactive.

There is a secondary invalidation risk in [native/src/scatter/mod.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/mod.rs:2319): `set_layout_rect()` intentionally keeps cached render targets valid for pure screen-position/scissor changes. ## Why The Prior Fix Did Not Solve It

The previous implementation added `cancel_scatter_interaction()` and expanded debug snapshots. That was useful for stale event routing, but the current screenshot and snapshot show:

- `active_scatter_id` is `null`.
- Left/right point counts, bounds, colormaps, and scalar-bar settings remain distinct.
- The visual failure still occurs because texture placement is wrong, not because plot data or widget ids are swapped.

So the bug is in GPU compositing state, not Python data reuse, widget id collision, or stale `active_scatter_id`.

## Other Places With The Same Defect Pattern

Direct same-defect pattern:

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1264) through [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1424): one `ScatterCompositeRenderer` with one mutable uniform buffer.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1426) through [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1492): each `ScatterRenderTarget` stores a bind group that references the shared uniform.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13687) through [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13818): visible scatter loop writes the shared uniform and composites each target.

Any view with two or more visible `Scatter3D`/`ScatterPlot2D` widgets can exhibit this when at least two are rendered through the cached/offscreen compositor path. Known affected surfaces:

- Professional demo `3D Explore`
- `examples/css_feature_probes/adjacent_scatter_interaction_probe.py`
- Any custom app with adjacent `Scatter3D` and/or `ScatterPlot2D`

Other renderers are probably not affected by this exact bug. The line plot and primitive renderers use their own render paths and do not use `ScatterCompositeRenderer`.

## Proposed Fix Approach

Fix the compositor so composite placement data is not a mutable singleton shared by all scatter composites in a frame.

Preferred implementation:

1. Move the composite uniform buffer from `ScatterCompositeRenderer` into `ScatterRenderTarget`.
2. Create each `ScatterRenderTarget` with:
   - its offscreen color/depth textures,
   - its own `wgpu::Buffer` for `ScatterCompositeUniforms`,
   - a bind group that binds that target-specific uniform buffer plus the target texture view and shared sampler.
3. Replace `ScatterCompositeRenderer::update_uniforms(...)` with either:
   - `ScatterRenderTarget::update_composite_uniforms(...)`, or
   - a compositor helper that accepts `&target.uniform_buffer`.
4. In the scatter render loop, update the current target's own uniform buffer before drawing `target.bind_group`.
5. Keep the pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared in `ScatterCompositeRenderer`; only the mutable per-draw placement data needs to move.

Acceptable alternatives:

- Use a dynamic uniform buffer with one aligned offset per visible scatter in the frame.
- Use immediate/push constants for `target_rect` and `screen_size` if supported cleanly by the current wgpu/backend constraints.

Verification should be pixel-based, not only debug-snapshot based:

- Force both adjacent scatters through the cached/offscreen compositor path.

- Rebuild and reinstall/copy `_dragongui.pyd` after the native change before rerunning the professional demo.

+## Root Cause
+
+The desktop/tablet panel failures were mostly caused by ambiguous pane sizing:
+
+- The demo used values like `Pane(size=0.7)` and `Pane(size=0.3)` intending proportions.
+- The Python API serialized numeric pane sizes as fixed pixels.
+- Native layout treated those as tiny fixed sizes, disabled flex growth, then clamped panes to `min_size`.
+- Splitters therefore used only the pane minimum widths and left hundreds of pixels blank.
+
+There was a second visible issue on the data page:
+
+- The demo passed `list[dict]` rows to `DataFrameTable`.
+- The dataframe adapter did not infer columns for that shape, so the table rendered row indices with no real data columns.

+Strong suspect in `native/src/runtime.rs`:

+- Scatter widgets may render into per-widget `ScatterRenderTarget`s and then composite those textures to the swapchain.
+- `ScatterCompositeRenderer` owns a single uniform buffer/bind group for `target_rect`.
+- During frame encoding, `self.scatter_compositor.update_uniforms(...)` is called once per scatter, then `render(...)` is called for that scatter.
+- Because command buffers reference the same uniform buffer, later `queue.write_buffer` calls can make all composite draws observe the last written `target_rect` instead of the per-draw rectangle.
+- This can cause one scatter texture, often the right-side plot, to be drawn over another plot's rectangle after cached/offscreen rendering is activated by interaction/redraw.

+- direct render vs cached render switching after clicks or interaction render scale changes;

+
+    def walk(node: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
+        nonlocal fallback
+        node_id = str(node.get("id") or "")
+        node_type = str(node.get("type") or "")
+        class_name = str(node.get("class") or "")

The previous fix addressed stale pointer state (`active_scatter_id`) but did not fix the remaining compositor bug. The scatter offscreen compositor stores the placement rectangle in one shared uniform buffer owned by `ScatterCompositeRenderer`, while each scatter render target has its own texture bind group that points back at that shared buffer.

- [examples/all_features_professional_demo.py](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/examples/all_features_professional_demo.py:579) creates the large left `Scatter3D`.

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1264) defines `ScatterCompositeRenderer`; [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1268) stores a single `uniform_buffer`.

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1426) defines `ScatterRenderTarget`; it stores only `bind_group`, dimensions, format, and revision, not a per-target/per-draw composite uniform.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1476) creates each render target bind group through the shared compositor.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13786) writes the current scatter widget's `target_rect` into the shared uniform buffer immediately before drawing that scatter target.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13800) starts the composite render pass, and [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13816) draws the target using that target's texture bind group.
- [native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl:26) uses `uniforms.target_rect` in the vertex shader to place the sampled target texture on screen.

Why this fails: multiple `queue.write_buffer` calls update the same uniform buffer while encoding a frame. The draw bind groups sample different per-widget textures, but all of them reference the same placement uniform resource. With two cached scatter widgets in one frame, later writes can make both composite draws use the last scatter's rectangle. That produces exactly the screenshot: the left scatter texture is sampled, but placed into the right scatter's rectangle, combining with the right plot.

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13698) routes render-scale cases through the offscreen target path.
- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:13700) also allows static full-scale cached targets to be composited, so the bug can appear even when debug state says interactions are inactive.

There is a secondary invalidation risk in [native/src/scatter/mod.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/scatter/mod.rs:2319): `set_layout_rect()` intentionally keeps cached render targets valid for pure screen-position/scissor changes. That is only safe if the compositor placement state is isolated per draw. With the shared uniform, position-only cache reuse makes the wrong-rectangle failure more visible.

## Why The Prior Fix Did Not Solve It

The previous implementation added `cancel_scatter_interaction()` and expanded debug snapshots. That was useful for stale event routing, but the current screenshot and snapshot show:

- `active_scatter_id` is `null`.
- Left/right point counts, bounds, colormaps, and scalar-bar settings remain distinct.

So the bug is in GPU compositing state, not Python data reuse, widget id collision, or stale `active_scatter_id`.

## Other Places With The Same Defect Pattern

Direct same-defect pattern:

- [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1264) through [native/src/runtime.rs](J:/Projects/DragonFrame/native/src/runtime.rs:1424): one `ScatterCompositeRenderer` with one mutable uniform buffer.

Any view with two or more visible `Scatter3D`/`ScatterPlot2D` widgets can exhibit this when at least two are rendered through the cached/offscreen compositor path. Known affected surfaces:

- Professional demo `3D Explore`
- `examples/css_feature_probes/adjacent_scatter_interaction_probe.py`
- Any custom app with adjacent `Scatter3D` and/or `ScatterPlot2D`

Other renderers are probably not affected by this exact bug. The line plot and primitive renderers use their own render paths and do not use `ScatterCompositeRenderer`.

## Proposed Fix Approach

Fix the compositor so composite placement data is not a mutable singleton shared by all scatter composites in a frame.

Preferred implementation:

1. Move the composite uniform buffer from `ScatterCompositeRenderer` into `ScatterRenderTarget`.
2. Create each `ScatterRenderTarget` with:
   - its offscreen color/depth textures,
   - its own `wgpu::Buffer` for `ScatterCompositeUniforms`,
   - a bind group that binds that target-specific uniform buffer plus the target texture view and shared sampler.
3. Replace `ScatterCompositeRenderer::update_uniforms(...)` with either:
   - `ScatterRenderTarget::update_composite_uniforms(...)`, or
   - a compositor helper that accepts `&target.uniform_buffer`.
4. In the scatter render loop, update the current target's own uniform buffer before drawing `target.bind_group`.
5. Keep the pipeline, bind-group layout, and sampler shared in `ScatterCompositeRenderer`; only the mutable per-draw placement data needs to move.

Acceptable alternatives:

- Use a dynamic uniform buffer with one aligned offset per visible scatter in the frame.
- Use immediate/push constants for `target_rect` and `screen_size` if supported cleanly by the current wgpu/backend constraints.

[[HANDOFF_TO_BUG_FIXER]]
Diagnosis is complete in `artifacts/DIAGNOSIS.md`.

Root cause: the remaining bug is not stale `active_scatter_id`; it is GPU scatter compositing. `ScatterCompositeRenderer` owns one shared `uniform_buffer` for `target_rect`, and every `ScatterRenderTarget` bind group references that same buffer. With two cached/offscreen scatter widgets in one frame, both draws can use the last-written rectangle, so the left plot texture gets drawn into the right plot area.

Key evidence:
- Reproduced in `artifacts/visual_audit/screenshots/adjacent-scatter-interaction-1120x720.png`.
- Snapshot shows both scatters have distinct data/state and `active_scatter_id=null`, but both are using cached/composite rendering.
- Relevant source: `native/src/runtime.rs:1264`, `1268`, `1384`, `13786`, `13816`; shader placement at `native/src/scatter/composite.wgsl:26`.

Proposed fix: move the composite uniform buffer into `ScatterRenderTarget` or otherwise make placement data per draw/per target. Keep compositor pipeline/layout/sampler shared, but do not share mutable placement uniforms across scatter targets. Verification must include pixel-based adjacent plot checks, since the existing pass marker only checks state and misses wrong on-screen placement.
[[END_HANDOFF]]
